items.title: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong- Gator & Ben interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 8, 2024
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...we would get excited that we were going to open up for any number of people, Rick Derringer or that kind of thing.

ctx.x: Typically, yeah. MR. Yeah. I just recall, I was in the rock business in the 80s and we would get excited that we were going to open up for any number of people, Rick Derringer or that kind of thing. And more often than not it was a drag. The people weren’t there to see us. We often times felt the sound man was making us sound not too good just in case — but do you ever get the sense that your audience is tired out after, you know you’re the third band? I mean when I look at your videos it looks like the flock is…

Yeah. No I mean I think a lot of it is a product of that kind of our general scene is that ever since I started seeing shows kind of in that rock/jam scene, you’re typically in for a marathon of a night you know. And it’s definitely a battle. There’s definitely times where we’ll adjust the set. You know if we’ll get towards kind of mid-second set and you can kind of get a vibe that people might be tiring out a little bit. Or if we’re playing more typically they’re full two-set shows, but if we’re playing on a…
